rulers.note: Provisional consuls 10 November to 12 December 1799: Bonaparte, Sieyès and Ducos; from 12 December 1799 Bonaparte First Consul, Cambacérès Second and Lebrun Third. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Consulate begins on 9 November 1799 ('the fall of the Directory in the coup of 18 Brumaire on 9 November 1799'), but Cliopatria's row starts in 1800. The land is taken to be the 1800 shape (Egypt still occupied, the Jura added) for the last seven weeks of 1799; the page gives no area and no territory.

keyframe_review.note: 671,882 km2 for 1800..1802, 2,745 cells: metropolitan France with Belgium (142), the left bank of the Rhine (Germany 104, Luxembourg 12, a Dutch edge, 13) and Geneva, plus 168 Egyptian cells (the Nile Delta and valley to Sohag) and a handful of overseas cells (Senegal 7, Mauritius 5, Côte d'Ivoire 4). Egypt: 'Napoleon left Egypt in August 1799'; 'Belliard's surrender in Cairo 27 June 1801'; 'Menou capitulated on 2 September' (the timeline says 31 August); the Capitulation of Alexandria repatriated the army. So the Egypt cells are right for 1800 and 1801 only (new keyframe 1802), and are land held by the army (the french-directory dossier records the conquest of 1798 as a gain). The Jura (4 cells) is missing from the shape although the Helvetic Republic page says France annexed the Prince-Bishopric of Basel; it is added. The page gives no area; the overseas cells and the Rhine-bank cells are unverified (page budget).

keyframe_review.note: 667,759 km2 for 1803..1804, 2,754 cells. It adds Piedmont and the Aosta valley (annexed 11 September 1802, Subalpine Republic page), Parma and Piacenza (French from 1802 on the Duchy of Parma page, formal annexation 1808), Elba (transferred to France in 1802 by the Peace of Amiens, Elba page) and Lomellina/Oltrepò edge cells (Pavia 11) with Ligurian and Tuscan edge cells that are outline noise or Piedmont's outliers. It also draws the Valais (20 of 21 cells), which the Canton of Valais page says was 'the separate Rhodanic Republic' from 1802 until annexed as the Simplon department in 1810: removed. The Jura is added as in 1800. The page gives no area.

ledger.note: 9 November 1799: the coup of 18 Brumaire makes Bonaparte First Consul. 'The Consulate ... was the top-level government of the First French Republic from the fall of the Directory in the coup of 18 Brumaire on 9 November 1799 until the start of the French Empire on 18 May 1804'; the new constitution was confirmed by a referendum on 7 February 1800. The page names no territory; the land is the Directory's, with Egypt still occupied.

region.text: the Helvetic Republic, Switzerland without Geneva, Neuchâtel and the Bishopric of Basel

ledger.note: November 1799: the Helvetic Republic stays France's client. Infobox 'Client state of France'; the 'treaty of alliance of 19 August [1798] with France'; French troops stayed until 'the withdrawal of French troops in July 1802' (Act of Mediation page). The relation began in April 1798 (french-directory dossier); the page does not mention the change of government.

14 June 1800: Marengo. 'At the Battle of Marengo on 14 June 1800, what briefly seemed like a potential defeat for France was' turned into victory by Desaix and Kellermann. The page does not name the land; Marengo lies in Piedmont, held by the Austrians since 1799.

region.text: northern Italy, where the war of 1800 was fought

ledger.note: 9 February 1801: the Treaty of Lunéville. 'The treaty was finally signed at 5:00 in the evening on 9 February 1801.' 'The entire left bank of the Rhine, including the Austrian Netherlands, was ceded to France'; 'The independence and sovereignty of the Cisalpine, Ligurian, Batavian and Helvetic republics was recognized'; 'Imperial Italy was also ceded by the Empire, becoming parts of France and the new Italian Republic'; Austria kept Venetia and Istria. The French Consulate page: Lunéville 'signed in February 1801'. The treaty page names no zone; Piedmont is the researcher's reading of the Italian front.

region.text: the Nile Delta and Nile valley held by the French army in Egypt

ledger.note: 8 March 1801: the British land at Aboukir. The page's timeline: '8 March (17 Ventôse year IX) - British landing near Aboukir'; 'Between 8 and 21 March the British won a series of victories over the French' at Abukir, Mandora and Alexandria; the British and Ottomans captured Cairo 'between April and June'.

region.text: Cairo and the Nile valley, without the Alexandria governorate

ledger.note: 27 June 1801: Cairo and the Nile valley are lost. The timeline gives '27 June 1801' for General Belliard's surrender in Cairo; the British and Ottomans captured Cairo 'between April and June'. The region (Egypt without Alexandria) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Alexandria, the last French holding in Egypt

ledger.note: 2 September 1801: Alexandria capitulates. 'Menou capitulated on 2 September' (the timeline gives 31 August); the Capitulation of Alexandria 'allowed the Army of the Orient to be repatriated to Europe in British ships'. The page does not say who took the land; the British and Ottomans did.

region.text: the Nile Delta and Nile valley held by the French army in Egypt

ledger.note: 2 September 1801: the fighting in Egypt ends with the capitulation of Alexandria; 'the campaign ultimately ended in failure, with 15,000 French troops killed in action and 15,000 by disease'.

1802: Elba passes to France. Elba page: 'In 1801, the Peace of Luneville gave Elba to the Kingdom of Etruria' and 'it was transferred to France in 1802 by the Peace of Amiens' (the Consulate page: 'The March 1802 Peace of Amiens'); the page gives no month for the transfer. Napoleon arrived there as sovereign on 4 May 1814.

region.text: the Duchy of Parma and Piacenza

ledger.note: 1802: Parma and Piacenza fall to France in fact. Duchy of Parma page: 'the Duke remained in Parma until he died in 1802' (no month), the Treaty of Aranjuez of 1801 'formally decided the cession of the duchy to France', and 'the formal annexation to the French Empire was declared only in 1808'. The page gives no date for the French takeover; 1802 is a bridge from the duke's death, and Cliopatria draws Parma and Piacenza French from 1803.

region.text: the départements of Doire, Marengo, Pô, Sesia, Stura and Tanaro: Piedmont and the Aosta valley, without Novara ("The Italian Republic received Novara, which became the department of Agogna") and the Ossola

ledger.note: 11 September 1802: Piedmont is annexed. 'The Subalpine Republic ceased to exist on 11 September 1802'; 'The French Republic annexed the départements of Doire, Marengo, Pô, Sesia, Stura, and Tanaro'. The Subalpine (Piedmontese) Republic had been declared on 10 September 1798, ended on 20 June 1799 under Austro-Russian conquest, and was 're-established on 20 June 1800'. The Kingdom of Sardinia page gives no month for the annexation.

region.text: the Helvetic Republic, Switzerland without Geneva, Neuchâtel and the Bishopric of Basel

ledger.note: 19 February 1803: the Helvetic Republic is abolished. 'On 19 February 1803, the Act of Mediation abolished the Helvetic Republic and restored the cantons' (Helvetic Republic page); the Mediation Confederation that replaced it is not recorded here as a client (the pages opened do not say).

wars.name: French campaign in Egypt and Syria

zones.text: the Nile Delta and Nile valley held by the French army in Egypt

wars.outcome: The French held Cairo and Lower Egypt from 1798 and reached Girga in Upper Egypt on 29 December 1798; Bonaparte left in August 1799; Kléber signed the Convention of El Arish on 24 January 1800 (rejected by Britain); the British landed on 8 March 1801, Belliard surrendered Cairo on 27 June and Menou capitulated at Alexandria on 2 September 1801. The Treaty of Paris of 25 June 1802 ended hostilities between France and the Ottoman Empire.
wars.note: The page does not mention a 'Treaty of Alexandria'; the Capitulation of Alexandria is the terminal act. 15,000 French killed in action and 15,000 by disease.

wars.name: Marengo campaign and Treaty of Lunéville
wars.outcome: Victory at Marengo on 14 June 1800; the Treaty of Lunéville of 9 February 1801 ceded the left bank of the Rhine to France, recognised the Cisalpine, Ligurian, Batavian and Helvetic republics and confirmed Austria in Venetia and Istria.
wars.note: The Consulate page dates Marengo (14 June 1800) and the treaty ('February 1801'); the treaty page dates it 9 February 1801. Hohenlinden and the other battles of the war are on no page opened.

certainty.note: French frontiers on the Rhine, in the Alps and in Italy follow treaty lines (Lunéville 1801) and the annexed départements. Exceptions: Egypt (soft, an occupation front to 2 September 1801), the overseas cells, and the Italian dependencies of 1802-1804.

notes: Cliopatria draws two shapes (1800..1802, 1803..1804) whose changes are: Egypt out (2 September 1801; Cliopatria keeps it to 1802), Piedmont and the Aosta valley in (11 September 1802), Parma and Piacenza in (1802, confidence 1), Elba in (1802), and the Valais in (Cliopatria; wrong: the Rhodanic Republic). A new keyframe covers 1799 (the Consulate begins 9 November 1799; Cliopatria starts 1800) and one 1802 (Egypt gone). The Jura (former Prince-Bishopric of Basel, annexed by France per the Helvetic Republic page) is added; Cliopatria gives it to the Helvetic Republic instead. Overseas cells in the shape (Senegal 7, Mauritius 5, Côte d'Ivoire 4) belong to the colonial empire; they are unverified (page budget: this dossier opened nine pages against a budget of 1-2 because the shapes bundle Egypt, Piedmont, Parma, Elba and the Valais). Not recorded for lack of an opened page: the Consulate's client relations with the restored Cisalpine Republic (June 1800) and the Italian Republic (Bonaparte president from 26 January 1802), the Ligurian and Batavian Republics, the Kingdom of Etruria (Aranjuez 1801), and the Valais as a French protectorate; the Louisiana retrocession (San Ildefonso, 1800) and sale (1803), Saint-Domingue and the other colonies (first-french-colonial-empire, french-louisiana and saint-domingue dossiers); the left bank of the Rhine was already French from the Directory (Campo Formio 1797) and Lunéville only confirms it. The Subalpine Republic (Piedmont, 1798-1799 and 1800-1802, French-controlled) needs a dossier. Infobox area: none on the page. The Consulate shares the umbrella entity (French Consulate) with French India in Cliopatria; no dossier for the umbrella. Undated: the transfer of Parma in 1802 (confidence 1); the month of the Peace of Amiens transfer of Elba.
